notes: Recorded 301 master's and 3 doctoral programme rows. The HEA publishes no course list: it says each institution decides which courses accept GOI-IES scholars (FAQ 14), so these rows are the lists that institutions publish themselves, not a complete national list.

Institutions with a published course list and rows recorded: Trinity College Dublin (142), University College Cork (16), University of Limerick (12), Atlantic Technological University (10), Dublin City University (33), Griffith College (9), Mary Immaculate College (6 master's, 3 doctoral), National College of Ireland (5 rows: 1 group plus 4 named), National College of Art and Design (3), University of Galway (34), Dublin Business School (28), Munster Technological University (3).

University of Limerick says all PhD areas at UL are eligible; Mary Immaculate College names three research programmes. DCU says GOI-IES is not applicable to postgraduate certificate, diploma or PhD study at DCU. No institution page read lists other doctoral courses.

University of Galway's list is headed 'Eligible Programmes 2027/2028' and says it changes each year; it is recorded because it is the list the university currently publishes. ATU's page says the programme is closed for 2026 and reopens in January 2027; NCAD's page says the opportunity is closed for 2026.

NCI: the page ranks priorities (any master's in the School of Business and Social Sciences, then four School of Computing master's); it is a shortlisting priority, not a course restriction, and NCI funds at most two scholarships.

DBS: the page says all DBS master's courses qualify; the 28 rows are the DBS master's courses on its international courses page. The one online course on that page (Digital Marketing and Analytics (Online)) is left out because the HEA does not accept online courses. The HEA requires full-time in-person study, so check the mode of each DBS course.
MTU: the Cork campus page names three programmes; MTU's other pages are not consistent about which programmes are eligible, so this list may be incomplete.

Trinity College Dublin names truncated in the PDF were completed only where the wording makes the full name certain (for example Chemistr to Chemistry, Comp Sci to Computer Science). 'Ageing Health and Wellbeing in Intellectual' is cut off in the source and is kept as printed.
Combined 'Graduate Diploma / master's' courses are recorded as one master's row with the source's own name.
not_stated: The HEA gives no list of eligible courses or subjects.

No course list was read for Maynooth University, University College Dublin, South East Technological University, Technological University Dublin, Technological University of the Shannon, Dundalk Institute of Technology, CCT College, Dun Laoghaire Institute of Art, Design and Technology, ICD Business School, Independent College or RCSI.

Technological University Dublin, Technological University of the Shannon, Dundalk Institute of Technology, CCT College, IADT, ICD Business School and RCSI: no page listing GOI-IES eligible courses was found on the institution's own site (the IADT page mentions GOI-IES for 2027 but names no eligible programme).
